stories.headline: Tesla to end Cybertruck production in 2027
stories.move: Musk said in a Nov. 9 X post that Tesla will stop building the Cybertruck in about eight months, after CNN reported Nov. 6 that Tesla plans to wind down production at its Austin plant. Musk said the factory space will go to the two-seat Cybercab robotaxi and that Tesla will "have to return deposits for a lot of people." Tesla doesn't disclose Cybertruck sales, but industry estimates cited by TechCrunch put total sales at about 71,000 since November 2023, short of the roughly 250,000 a year Musk once projected.
stories.why: Tesla is reallocating a flagship but underperforming product line to robotaxi production, the business Musk has staked much of Tesla's future valuation on.
stories.bear: Musk says Cybertruck isn't unprofitable, so ending it trades away existing revenue for a robotaxi ramp that is still unproven at scale.
stories.watch: How many Cybertrucks Tesla builds and sells before the line shuts down, and the pace of Cybercab production that replaces it.

stories.headline: AMD falls 8.8% in Nvidia-linked chip selloff
stories.move: AMD shares fell 8.75% to close at $534.06 on Friday, Nov. 13, giving back earlier gains as a sector-wide AI chip selloff deepened, Stock Titan and The Motley Fool reported. The slide came amid continued uncertainty over Nvidia's leadership following CEO Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation; the Fool said AMD was "caught in the downdraft stemming from uncertainty surrounding Nvidia."
stories.why: Even a chipmaker with its own strong results isn't immune when doubts about the dominant AI player's leadership unsettle the whole sector.
stories.bear: AMD's own business hasn't changed; the drop reflects sector sentiment rather than any new problem at the company.
stories.watch: Whether chip stocks stabilize once Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results Nov. 17.

stories.headline: Dell falls as AI-server selloff deepens
stories.move: Dell Technologies shares fell 8.16% to around $340.87 as of 10:05 a.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 13, GuruFocus reported, as a selloff in AI-server stocks deepened following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation. The report said Dell builds most of its AI servers on Nvidia hardware, tying its order outlook to confidence in Nvidia.
stories.why: Dell's AI server business depends heavily on Nvidia chips, so doubts about Nvidia's leadership flow straight into how investors price Dell's biggest growth line, days before its next earnings report.
stories.bear: Dell has already guided to about $19 billion of AI server revenue this quarter regardless of who runs Nvidia, and the stock remains up sharply for the year.
stories.watch: Dell's fiscal third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 24.

stories.headline: Arm falls on report tied to Nvidia's CEO search
stories.move: Arm Holdings shares fell 4.63% to $190.53 on Friday, Nov. 13, The Motley Fool reported, as chip stocks kept reacting to Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO. The report cited the Financial Times saying Nvidia's board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about potentially succeeding Huang; Arm's board told CNBC it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates."
stories.why: A move by Haas would leave SoftBank's Arm, chaired by Masayoshi Son, searching for its own new chief executive at the same time Nvidia is.
stories.bear: Nothing has been confirmed about Haas leaving Arm, and the drop may simply reflect the broader chip-sector pullback rather than company-specific news.
stories.watch: Any formal statement from Arm or Nvidia on Nvidia's permanent CEO search.

stories.headline: Broadcom falls as chip-sector selling widens
stories.move: Broadcom shares fell 4.76% on Friday, Nov. 13, StockTitan reported, as selling tied to Nvidia's leadership upheaval spread beyond Nvidia and AMD to Broadcom. The report gave no company-specific cause for the move.
stories.why: Broadcom's size and AI-chip exposure make it one of the first stocks investors sell when sentiment turns on the sector, even without news of its own.
stories.bear: Broadcom has had no negative company-specific news this week, and the move may reverse quickly once sentiment stabilizes.
stories.watch: Broadcom's fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year results, due Dec. 9.

watch: Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results Nov. 17, with the board still searching for a permanent CEO.
Dell Technologies reports fiscal third-quarter results Nov. 24.
Broadcom reports fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year results Dec. 9.
quickHits: Nvidia's market value briefly slipped back under $4 trillion during Friday's selloff before the stock pared losses to close down about 2%, extending its longest weekly losing streak since 2012, Yahoo Finance reported.
memo: When a dominant supplier's leadership gets shaky, don't assume the damage stays contained — Friday's chip selloff shows how fast that uncertainty spreads to everyone who depends on it.
Tesla is cutting a flagship product, the Cybertruck, to free up capacity for a bigger bet on robotaxis — a reminder that sunk cost shouldn't keep a struggling line alive.
A stock move isn't always about the company itself — four chipmakers fell Friday on one competitor's leadership news, not their own results.

movers.why: AMD fell 8.8% as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation dragged down AI chip stocks.
Dell fell 7.2% as an AI-server sell-off deepened after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
